bundle.build: npm run build: PASS (vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build)

environment: Chrome recipient and Codex in-app-browser sender with separate secure-cookie sessions; fixed Vue dist through a localhost HTTP/WebSocket reverse proxy to Go API; PostgreSQL 16 isolated schema; two synthetic DM participants and one synthetic nonparticipant; no LiveKit or production data

checks.name: nonparticipant_http_acl
checks.detail: A third login-issued session received HTTP 404 for the pair's DM history and scoped search.

checks.name: private_create_hint_and_unread
checks.detail: Both participant browsers showed online presence through the proxied WebSocket. A new DM from the sender updated the recipient's navigation badge to 1 and page title to (1) Voice Platform without a reload. Opening the DM showed the message and cleared the badge/title.

checks.name: private_edit_delete_hints
checks.detail: While the recipient viewed the DM, a sender edit appeared without reload and did not increase unread/title. A subsequent API-issued synthetic create and delete each updated the recipient's open history without reload; the deleted body disappeared and the row became a deletion marker. The API delete returned 204.

checks.name: browser_notification_delivery
checks.detail: Chrome displayed an available Enable notifications control, but enabling browser permission requires user confirmation and was not performed. Hidden-tab OS notification count, generic preview and duplicate suppression were therefore not observed.

checks.name: fixture_cleanup
checks.detail: The fixture reported CLEAN. Zero qa03_browser schemas remained; ports 18083 and 18769 had no listeners. Temporary credentials, attachment directory, scripts and binaries were removed.

limitations: The sender's native delete confirmation blocked in-app-browser automation, so a second synthetic message was deleted through the same authenticated API route while the recipient browser observed the realtime result.
The third participant's WebSocket delivery was not observed in a browser; server-side directed-event integration tests cover recipient filtering.
The bundle was locally built from a pinned source commit, not published by the trusted release pipeline; QA-03 and QA-05 remain open.
